name: Eneabba Rare Earths Refinery
location_description: Eneabba, Western Australia (brownfields site at Iluka's existing Eneabba operation)
description: Australia's first fully integrated rare-earths refinery (Eneabba Phase 3): roasting, leaching, purification, solvent extraction and product finishing, producing separated Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb oxides. FID 3 Apr 2022; capital cost A$1,000-1,200M; modelled TREO capacity 17.5 ktpa (23 ktpa nameplate with all circuits). Owned and operated via Iluka wholly-owned SPE 'RefineryCo'. Fed initially from Iluka's own Eneabba monazite/xenotime stockpile (indicative 9-year life on stockpile alone); designed to also process Iluka's Wimmera and other deposits and third-party concentrates. Start: FID targeted first production in 2025; the NTU DFS schedule (Fig 37, p.63) shows refinery completion mid-2027, and NTU describes the refinery as under construction (Sep 2025). Iluka identifies rare-earth metallisation as a potential future step.

name: USA Rare Earth Wheat Ridge Separation Facility
description: Separation capability that has demonstrated production of commercial-grade Dy and NdPr oxide from recycled feed. Future Serra Verde concentrates are described as part of the planned oxide-production feedstock base; commercial scale not established from public disclosures.

name: Less Common Metals
description: Rare-earth metal and alloy producer through which USA Rare Earth operates its metallization capability.

name: USA Rare Earth Stillwater Magnet Facility
description: First commercial sintered NdFeB magnet-production line commissioned in March 2026. Aerospace and defense are among the stated target markets.
